title: CAT 2024 Question Paper (Slot 3, QA) - Quant - Linear Quadratic
subject: Quant

questions.q: For some constant real numbers $p, k$ and ${a}$, consider the following system of linear equations in ${x}$ and ${y}$ :\n$$ \begin{aligned} & p x-4 y=2 \\ & 3 x+k y=a \end{aligned} $$\nA necessary condition for the system to have no solution for $(x, y)$, is:
questions.explain:
For a system of linear equations to have no solution, the lines must be parallel and distinct. This means the ratio of coefficients of x and y must be equal, but not equal to the ratio of the constant terms. The condition is $ rac{p}{3} =  rac{-4}{k} 
eq  rac{2}{a}$. From the inequality, we get $ak 
eq -12$ and $ap 
eq 6$. From the equality we get $pk = -12$. The condition $2a+k 
eq 0$ is a necessary condition for no solution.

questions.q: If $(a+b \sqrt{3})^2=52+30 \sqrt{3}$, where ${a}$ and ${b}$ are natural numbers, then $a+b$ equals:
questions.explain: Expanding the left side gives $(a^2 + 3b^2) + 2ab\sqrt{3}$. Comparing with the right side, we have $a^2 + 3b^2 = 52$ and $2ab = 30$, so $ab = 15$. By testing integer pairs for $ab=15$ (e.g., a=5, b=3), we find $5^2 + 3(3^2) = 25 + 27 = 52$. So $a=5$ and $b=3$. Thus, $a+b=8$.
